panels.title: 1. Double-entry
panels.body: Every transaction is recorded twice, as a debit and an equal credit, so the books always balance.
panels.ex: Buy a $500 laptop with cash: equipment up $500, cash down $500.

panels.title: 2. Accrual accounting
panels.body: Revenue and expenses are recorded when they are earned or incurred, not when the cash moves.
panels.ex: A $2,000 job finished in March and paid in April is March revenue.

panels.title: 3. Matching principle
panels.body: An expense is recorded in the same period as the revenue it helps to earn.
panels.ex: Stock bought for $600 in April and sold in May: the $600 cost goes in May.

panels.title: 4. Depreciation
panels.body: The cost of a long-lived asset is spread over the years the business uses it.
panels.ex: A $30,000 van used for 5 years with no resale value: $6,000 a year.

panels.title: 5. Working capital
panels.body: Current assets minus current liabilities: the cushion for day-to-day running.
panels.ex: $80,000 of current assets minus $50,000 of current liabilities = $30,000.
